summary: SSE stream becomes silent after initial chunks when clients reconnect through corporate proxy
description:
Issue summary: Multiple customers (initial report from BrightLedger) observe Server-Sent Events (SSE) streams that deliver the first 1-3 token chunks then become silent for 10s-90s and eventually time out. This started for BrightLedger after a routine edge proxy rollout on 2026-03-09. Impact: production chat features degrade (clients see partial responses followed by long silence or final 504). Affected sessions often involve clients sitting behind corporate HTTP proxies that re-establish connections (keepalive churn / pooled HTTP/2->HTTP/1.1 translation).

Observed behavior: SSE connection appears open (200 OK) and initial chunks are delivered; server-side trace shows continued generation and token emission, but client-side receives no more chunk boundaries. Some streams complete silently with last_event_id unchanged; others close with connection reset after idle timeout.

Expected behavior: SSE streams should continuously deliver chunks as they are generated until a final event indicates completion or an explicit error.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer uses Redwood chat SSE endpoint (POST /v1/chat/stream) from behind a corporate proxy that does HTTP/2 fronting and translates to HTTP/1.1 to the edge.
2) Start a long response (context ~6k tokens) which triggers progressive token emission and KV cache usage.
3) Introduce an artificial client reconnect pattern (short socket recycle / proxy pool rotation) or wait for normal proxy churn.
4) Observe initial 1-3 SSE chunks delivered, then silence despite server-side active generation logs.
5) Reproduce reliably for BrightLedger client by toggling proxy keepalive to simulate pooling behavior (customer-provided steps attached).
logs_and_traces: Edge request id: req-0a3f9c (BrightLedger session) - 2026-03-09T18:12:33Z - initial chunks sent up to event id 2 then no further chunk frames observed on wire
Serving runtime trace: span srv-7234 - generator continued producing token batches for another 38s; last write syscall shows EPIPE after socket re-use
NGINX edge logs: 2026-03-09T18:12:33Z client 10.0.1.5 upstream prematurely closed keepalive connection (pool)
tcpdump capture (attached): shows downstream client acking initial packets then zero-window updates during later frames when server tries to send larger chunked frames
investigation_notes: 03/10 09:15 - Triage: Confirmed reproducible with BrightLedger repro steps. Behavior correlates with a recent edge-proxy change that enabled HTTP/2 connection coalescing for upstreams (rollout 2026-03-09).

Hypothesis A: Proxy pooling / HTTP/2->HTTP/1.1 translation is causing flow-control window resets or connection re-use semantics that interrupt chunked SSE delivery even though server still believes socket is open.

Hypothesis B: Edge batching optimization aggregated small token frames into larger writev calls; when an intermediate proxy imposes backpressure the kernel leaves the socket in a state where subsequent writes return but are not delivered to client (zero-window), eventually causing stalls.
03/11 02:40 - Reproduced in staging by enabling the same coalescing flag; saw the same pattern. Disabling coalescing in staging returned normal continuous SSE delivery.

03/11 11:05 - Additional data: affected sessions have intermittent small gaps (<200ms) prior to stall, suggesting a timing-sensitive interaction with pool rotation. No evidence of model-side slowdown (generation CPU/GPU metrics normal).
Logs tied to upstream Nginx instance show KEEPALIVE resources returned to pool while server continues to write causing SIGPIPE in some worker connections.
customer_communication: 2026-03-10 09:40 - Carlos: Acknowledged receipt, opened ticket, requested repro steps and sample request ids. Promised first response within SLA.
2026-03-10 10:20 - BrightLedger Support (Elena Kovac): Provided proxy config, reproduction script, and a tcpdump capture. Customer requests a fast workaround as chat feature is used in demos.
2026-03-11 12:00 - Aisha: Confirmed it's a high priority, shared temporary mitigation (use websocket streaming or allow keepalive: timeout increase) and we are testing edge revert.
2026-03-12 16:30 - BrightLedger: Applied websocket fallback and reported reduced incidence, but still asking for a permanent fix and postmortem.
workaround: Short-term mitigation suggested to customer: switch to websocket streaming endpoint (ws://) for affected clients or configure corporate proxies to preserve connection affinity and increase keepalive / idle timeout. Engineering recommended disabling HTTP/2->1 coalescing on edge for the customer routing policy as an immediate server-side mitigation.
resolution_plan: 1) Roll back HTTP/2 connection coalescing flag on edge for all affected routes (in progress). 2) Add additional socket write backpressure monitoring and a fast-fail path in the edge-proxy to surface broken pooled connections to the generator (RCA and code change ticket to follow). 3) Create automated test that exercises proxy pooling and HTTP/2->1 translation for SSE and websockets. 4) Postmortem and customer follow-up with timeline and permanent fix. Estimated ETA for rollback and customer confirmation: 2026-03-13.
follow_up_actions: Engineering to create code PR to detect stalled pooled sockets and force connection close: owner @edge-team (ETA 2026-03-17)
SRE to monitor SSE error rate and customer 5xx/timeout counts across us-west-2 for 72 hours post-rollback
Support to update BrightLedger with rollback confirmation and provide postmortem link
comments: Aisha Patel (03/11): Confirmed staging repro and rolled edge flag back in staging. Preparing customer impact bulletin.
SRE (03/11): Noted an increase in SSE idle timeouts correlated with edge change; setting up additional tcpdump captures for production validation.
Carlos Mendoza (03/12): Rolled mitigation to BrightLedger routing and asked for websocket failover docs to be provided to their engineering team.
BrightLedger - Elena (03/12): Confirmed websocket fallback reduces occurrences; awaiting full fix and postmortem.
